title: Adaptive hinting + prefetch playtest notes
body:
Context and goal:
This is a focused playtest log for a small, iterative experiment: add adaptive prefetch hinting that reacts to observed reuse and memory-bandwidth pressure to reduce paging and long-tail latency. Goal is to find lightweight heuristics we can prototype in runtime v0.34 without a heavy predictor model.

Why this is different from prior notes: most previous artifacts looked at eviction heuristics and static prefetch windows. This doc captures short-running playtests that dynamically adjust prefetch aggressiveness per-tenant/instance based on reuse signal and instantaneous DRAM bandwidth headroom. Emphasis on operational observables and simple safety fallbacks.

Summary of approach (sketch):
- Collect per-request KV reuse signal: fraction of tokens that hit the cache vs miss (sampled at 1% of requests).
- Maintain a short sliding window (N=100 requests or 30s) of reuse_rate and observed page-in latency percentile (p95_pgi_ms).
- Also measure host memory bandwidth (sampled from perf counters) to compute bandwidth_headroom = max_bw - current_bw.
- Prefetch hint strength S ∈ {0,1,2,3} representing how many pages ahead we ask allocator to warm: 0=off, 3=aggressive.
- Rules (simple):
  * If reuse_rate > 0.6 and p95_pgi_ms > 20ms and bandwidth_headroom > 25% => increase S by 1 (capped at 3).
  * If reuse_rate < 0.2 or bandwidth_headroom < 10% => decrease S by 1 (floored at 0).
  * If consecutive misses spike (miss_rate delta > 0.15 in 5s) => immediate S=3 for 10s to reduce tail while we ramp.
- Safety: bounded increase rate (one step per 30s) and emergency fallback: if host OOM killer or swap activity detected, immediately set S=0.

Playtest hardware and workload:
- Testbed: 8x A100 (40GB) slice, instance type rw-staging-8x-a100-40.
- OS kernel: 6.1.22, nvme root, NUMA: 2 sockets.
- Workloads:
  * synth-longcontext: 10k requests, seq_len distribution: {256:30%, 1024:50%, 2048:20%}, multimodal mix of chat and code-gen.
  * multi-tenant-noise: 4 tenants, skewed QPS (0.6/0.2/0.15/0.05) with tenant 1 heavy reuse, tenant 4 random.
  * bursty-batch: 5000 bursty concurrent small requests to stress prefetch decisions.

Key metrics captured (sampled at 1s granularity):
- kv_hit_rate_sampled, kv_miss_rate, p50_pgi_ms, p95_pgi_ms, bytes_prefetched, prefetched_pages_evicted_before_use, host_mem_bw_util_pct, pagefault_rate, tail_latency_99.

Results (selected observations):
1) synth-longcontext baseline (S=0 always):
   - sampled_reuse_rate ~ 0.42
   - p95_pgi_ms = 26ms
   - tail_latency_99 = 540ms
   - host_mem_bw_util = 62%
2) static aggressive prefetch (S=3 static):
   - reuse_rate 0.47 (+5pp), p95_pgi_ms = 14ms (improved), tail_latency_99 = 380ms
   - bytes_prefetched increased +48%
   - prefetched_pages_evicted_before_use = 12% (worse under multi-tenant)
   - host_mem_bw_util = 84% (dangerous close to saturation)
3) adaptive hinting (rules above):
   - average S ~ 1.4 (varies per tenant), reuse_rate observed 0.45
   - p95_pgi_ms = 16ms, tail_latency_99 = 400ms (close to static aggressive)
   - bytes_prefetched +22% (better efficiency than static)
   - prefetched_pages_evicted_before_use = 4% (significant reduction)
   - host_mem_bw_util = 70% (safe margin)
4) multi-tenant-noise drama: when tenant 1 hogged queue and tenant 4 noisy, static S=3 led to sharp bw saturation and eviction of prefetched pages for low-QPS tenants -> miss spikes. Adaptive scheme kept S low for noisy tenants and high for tenant1 (per-tenant state), preventing global saturation.

Micro-observations and surprises:
- Prefetch eviction before use correlated strongly with host bw_util > 78% and with high interleaving churn (multiple tenants) — not just reuse_rate alone.
- Short windows (N=100 requests) can misclassify bursty tenants; added exponential backoff on S decreases to avoid oscillation.
- We observed a class of cold pages that were prefetched but evicted due to the eviction policy not honoring recent prefetch hints; need an eviction-weight bump for prefetched pages for 2s to allow use.
- Page-in p95 is a good fast signal but p99 remains noisy; safety rules must still handle p99 spikes.

Small ASCII table: (aggregated across runs)

scenario | avg_S | p95_pgi_ms | tail_p99_ms | prefetched_bytes_delta | bw_util
baseline | 0.0   | 26ms       | 540ms       | 0%                     | 62%
adaptive | 1.4   | 16ms       | 400ms       | +22%                   | 70%
static3  | 3.0   | 14ms       | 380ms       | +48%                   | 84%

Actionable notes / next experiments:
- Add per-prefetch soft-priority that increments eviction score (prefetch_score) so prefetched pages get a short grace period of 1.5-2s. Measure effect on prefetched_pages_evicted_before_use. (JIRA-ENG-2187)
- Replace crude bandwidth_headroom with a rolling percentile projection (10s window) to reduce sensitivity to short bursts.
- Test adaptive scheme with larger multi-tenant mixes (10 tenants) and on lower-memory GPUs (e.g., 48GB V100) to see if behavior generalizes.
- Run with sequence-length-aware hinting: longer seqs => prefetch farther ahead (S step mapping to seq_len). Hypothesis: will improve reuse without extra bw.
- Investigate hooking hint strength to model/kernel selection planner so that heavyweight kernels that tend to cause bigger page-ins get higher S.

Implementation notes (runtime changes to prototype):
- Small patch in page_warmup_manager: add hint_strength per allocation group, persisted in allocation metadata, exposed via /internal/telemetry.
- perf counters read via libperf sampled at 250ms; we average to 1s buckets.
- Sampling: only 1% of requests traced for reuse to reduce overhead. Consider stratified sampling by seq_len.

Open questions and risks:
- Does increasing prefetch for one tenant bias eviction unfairly across NUMA nodes? Need NUMA-aware hint targeting.
- Can tenants game heuristics (e.g., synthetic high reuse patterns) to get more bandwidth? Consider quota enforcement.
- Operational: adding many per-tenant states increases memory; need to LRU the per-tenant hint table.

Quick TODOs (short horizon):
- [ ] Land prefetch_score grace-period bump and run overnight multi-tenant test (owner: Miguel).
- [ ] Add rolling-percentile bandwidth estimator and compare hysteresis thresholds (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Add telemetry dashboards: per-tenant avg_S, prefetched_evicted_pct, host_bw_util (owner: Jamal).
- [ ] Write short explainer for product: how adaptive prefetch avoids tail regressions (owner: Asha).

Notes to self: keep heuristic small and auditable. If a ML predictor is needed later, use the heuristics as warm-start labels. Save raw logs for one week: /var/log/serving/kv-prefetch-playtest-2025-02-11.log (archived to s3://rw-inference-playtests).

Appended raw sample (one-minute snapshot):
- timestamp: 2025-02-11T14:12:00Z
- avg_S: 1.1
- sampled_reuse_rate: 0.51
- p95_pgi_ms: 15.2ms
- host_mem_bw_util: 68%
- bytes_prefetched_rate: 12MB/s
- prefetched_pages_evicted_before_use: 3%

If this looks promising I propose we fold adaptive hinting into the next canary rollout (runtime v0.34-canary) behind a feature flag; monitor tenant-level bw_util and prefetched_evicted_before_use, with auto-disable if bw_util > 88% for >30s.

References and linked tickets: JIRA-ENG-2187 (design), PR #542 (prototype), confluence:kv-prefetch-design-v2.

End of playtest notes.
